# Local continuity of catalogue declarations

The question is whether accession and creator context improves the recovery of a hidden label beyond the continuity already encoded by adjacent inventory IDs. Ordered ingest can make a record's neighbors informative even if they have a different creator or accession. Treat Object ID as an observed catalogue index. Its numeric order does not establish acquisition chronology. The prediction is a retrospective quality-control score for the literal Met declaration.

Use the same training and development objects as the first screen. Keep SHA-256 buckets 80–99 reserved. For each query use only the labels of the designated training reference rows. Build training predictors with five-way cross-fitting using the original hash folds. Derive left and right windows of 1, 4 and 16 labeled records under three orders: global ID, ID within accession family, and ID within artist. Use smoothed directional rates, ID gap, observed count, and an indicator that the nearest labeled records agree. Missing keys yield no group neighbors. Every learned predictor uses CatBoost on GPU with the same iterations, depth, shrinkage and seed. Give every fit the raw inventory ID and original metadata.

Compare metadata alone, the earlier family/artist/joint nearest-neighbor features, metadata plus global windows, metadata plus family/artist windows, and their full union with the earlier features. Additionally compare a simple global two-sided local mean with window size selected using training cross-fit loss. Save development predictions for every comparator and the training-only window choice. The prespecified development screen for this iteration is a reduction in pooled mean log loss of at least .005 nats against every alternative. Report ties and losses. This is method selection under artificial item masking, with no claim of superiority on unseen collections. Reused development data cannot confirm publication eligibility.
